realism.how: An electric centrifugal juicer, mains powered, bought new at the state department store or the household-goods shop (Czechoslovak and East German factories made them in plastic and enamel). A kiosk or market stall that sells juice by the glass used a stainless commercial centrifuge or a glass-cone juice dispenser like the state groceries had.
realism.current: Every 1989 kitchen and juice kiosk had an electric one; a hand-cranked wooden press was what a grandmother kept in the barn for the autumn cider. A local would read the electric machine as normal, the press as antique.
